definition.text: An indicator, built from the IUCN Red List, that tracks how the extinction risk of whole groups of species changes over time.

facts.text: Repeating conservation assessments at regular intervals lets changes in species' threat status reveal trends in extinction risk.
It can be broken down by taxonomic group, biogeographic realm, habitat type or main threat.
A sampled version (SRLI) assesses a representative sample of species, since assessing every fungus, insect and plant is impractical.
The shark and ray Red List Index has fallen 19% since the 1970s because of overfishing.
Australia's national bird RLI fell from 0.927 in 1990 to 0.896 in 2020, picking up both the 2019–2020 wildfires and conservation successes.
It is the single indicator for Sustainable Development Goal target 15.5 and was used for the CBD's 2010 biodiversity target.
